title: The newton as a unit of force
canonical_question: What is one newton of force in terms of mass and acceleration?
summary: One newton is the force that gives a one-kilogram mass an acceleration of one metre per second squared.
Roughly, holding a small apple against gravity takes about one newton.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Defined by F = ma
sections.body_md: One newton is the force that gives a one-kilogram mass an acceleration of one metre per second squared. It comes straight from F = ma with the numbers set to one. So a newton is a kilogram-metre per second squared.

sections.heading: A feel for the size
sections.body_md: Roughly, holding a small apple against gravity takes about one newton. Everyday pushes are a few to a few hundred newtons. Knowing this keeps your force answers sensible.

key_points: One newton accelerates 1 kg at 1 m/s^2.
About the weight of a small apple.
core.bridge_to_parent: It clarifies the unit implied by the objective’s law.
